text: Quick checklist BEFORE filing a patent application: 1) Prior art search completed (TKDL, patent databases, publications). 2) Novelty and inventive step confirmed. 3) Section 3 analysis done (d/e/j/p relevance assessed). 4) NBA Form III submitted (if biological resources). 5) Invention documented with dates (lab notebooks). 6) Professional patent search/opinion obtained (recommended). 7) Budget allocated (filing + prosecution + renewals). 8) International strategy decided (PCT vs direct filing).

Patent claim writing tips for AYUSH: 1) Start broad, narrow in dependent claims. 2) Use 'comprising' for open-ended claims, 'consisting of' for closed. 3) Define ranges (e.g., 5-20% w/w) not single values. 4) Cover both product and process where possible. 5) Include pharmaceutical composition and method of treatment claims. 6) Use alternative language ('selected from the group'). 7) Avoid terms in TKDL texts. 8) Support every element with specification disclosure. 9) Get professional review before filing.

Most common patent rejection reasons for AYUSH applications: 1) Lack of novelty over TKDL/prior art — distinguish clearly. 2) Section 3(p) traditional knowledge — show innovation beyond. 3) Section 3(d) no enhanced efficacy — provide comparative data. 4) Section 3(e) mere admixture — show synergy with data. 5) Insufficient disclosure — add examples, working. 6) Claims not supported by description — align claims and spec. 7) Unclear claims — improve clarity, define terms. Address these proactively in your application.

Trade secret protection — DOs: Use NDAs before ANY disclosure. Limit access to need-to-know basis. Mark confidential documents clearly. Maintain access logs. Train employees on confidentiality. Use exit interviews with confidentiality reminders. DON'Ts: Share secrets without NDA (even verbally). Give broad access to sensitive information. Publish or present secret information. Ignore departing employee procedures. Leave confidential documents unattended. Assume trust replaces legal protection.

Trademark selection tips for AYUSH products: DO choose: Invented words (Ayushmax), Suggestive marks (Herbwell), Distinctive combinations (NaturaCure). DON'T choose: Generic terms (Ayurvedic Tablets), Descriptive terms (Herbal Health Tonic), Geographic names (Kerala Herbs) unless GI, Religious symbols (offensive to communities). Search before finalizing: TM Registry, domain availability, social handles. Unique marks are easier to protect and register.

IP portfolio management best practices: 1) Maintain IP register (all rights, dates, renewals). 2) Set calendar reminders 3 months before deadlines. 3) Review portfolio annually — prune non-valuable assets. 4) Monitor competitors' filings in your space. 5) Document all innovations (even if not patenting). 6) Budget for IP (filing + prosecution + maintenance). 7) Ensure proper assignment from employees/contractors. 8) Keep renewal payments current. 9) Review coverage before product launches. 10) Consider IP insurance for valuable assets.
